subject: general
question: Who among the following introduced the silver tanka and the copper Jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?
solution:
The correct answer is __Iltumish.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iltutmish **introduced the** Silver Tanka and Copper Jital, the two coins of the Delhi Sultanate.**
 
• The coins prior to Iltutmish were** introduced by the Rulers which bear the Sanskrit characters and even Bull and Shivalinga.**
 
• Iltutmish was the first to introduce a **“Pure Arabic Coin” in India.**
 
• The Coins were engraved with** “The Mighty Sultan, Sun of the Empire and the Faith, Conquest-laden, Iltumish,”** after he received an investiture of **Sovereign Sultan of Delhi from the Caliph of Baghdad.**
 
• The Silver Tanka issued by **Iltutmish was weighing 175 grains.**
 
• **Gold Tanka **of the same** weight was later issued by Balban.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Name

 Significant Contributions or Events
 
 
 
 

 Alauddin Khilji
 Khilji Dynasty
 1296 - 1316 AD
 Known for his market reforms and military campaigns. He successfully repelled the Mongol invasions and expanded his territory.
 
 

 Iltutmish
 Slave Dynasty (also known as Mamluk Dynasty)
 1211 - 1236 AD
 Consolidated the Delhi Sultanate and made Delhi the capital instead of Lahore. He introduced the silver Tanka and the copper Jital, the two basic coins of the Sultanate period.
 
 

 Ibrahim Lodi
 Lodi Dynasty
 1517 - 1526 AD
 Last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, remembered for his defeat and death at the hands of Babur in the first battle of Panipat, which marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
 

 Qutubuddin Aibak
 Slave Dynasty (also known as Mamluk Dynasty)
 1206 - 1210 AD
 He laid the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate and the Mamluk Dynasty. Known for commissioning the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
